relevantRules.Article4: An established rule-of-law breach must sufficiently directly affect or seriously risk EU-budget sound financial management or financial interests; procurement, financial control and effective judicial review are specified channels.
relevantRules.Article5: Measure design follows the relevant budget-management setting and is proportionate to impact/nature/duration/gravity/scope, targeting affected EU actions insofar as possible. Under paragraph2, programme/payment obligations to final recipients remain unless the adopting decision provides otherwise.
relevantRules.Article6: Reasoned Commission notification, opportunity for state observations/remedies, assessment and proportionality observations precede a reasoned Commission proposal where conditions remain met; a Council implementing decision is distinct from proposal or allegation.

claimLimits: Not every rule-of-law violation meets the required EU-budget link. Serious risk can suffice without an already realised loss.
High public debt by itself is not a rule-of-law breach or sufficient condition for payment suspension.
Article5(2) has the stated adopting-decision qualification; no universal unconditional beneficiary promise is made.
Teaching examples are fictional; the note is not a finding about any real member state or actual suspension.
No full extracted legal text is stored as a project artifact.
fiscalLawTreatment: No new fiscal-rule competence is created. The current whole753 fiscal-rule contract is reused for that already covered facet if needed; these fresh EMU cases use given fictional refinancing/rate/risk data only and assert no enacted fund, bailout, SGP sanction or old fiscal threshold. The2024/1263 page was opened for orientation; no article-level reading or fiscal-law review is claimed here.
